title: Line regulation: untrimmed output shift across the full 3.3 V +/-10% supply range
claim: README.md 'Target specification (DRAFT)' row 'Supply' (3.3 V +/-10%) read as an output-shift requirement, checked against the only bound the draft spec implies without inventing a number: the supply-induced shift must fit inside the entire +/-1% output-accuracy window (24 mV p-p on 1.20 V). NECESSARY, not sufficient -- a real budget gives line regulation a fraction of that window. Setting a dedicated line-regulation line item is issue #1's call; these numbers are its input. Records are PROVISIONAL against the draft spec until #1 ratifies it.

analyses: meas dc vrefnom FIND v(vref) AT=3.3

measurements.name: line_shift_mv
measurements.note: Peak-to-peak VREF excursion across 2.97..3.63 V. Limit is the full +/-1% output-accuracy window (24 mV on 1.20 V) -- see the claim: necessary, not sufficient, and not a ratified line-regulation number.

measurements.name: line_reg_pct_per_v
measurements.note: Informational (no limit): the same excursion expressed as a fractional output change per volt of supply, normalized to VREF at the nominal 3.30 V. The conventional way to quote line regulation.

measurements.name: line_psrr_db
measurements.note: Informational (no limit): large-signal DC supply rejection, 20*log10(dVDD/dVREF) over the full range. This is the independent counterpart of sim/psrr-dc/'s small-signal 0.1 Hz psrr_dc; the two should agree within a few dB, and a large disagreement means one of the two benches is wrong.

measurements.name: vref_nom
measurements.note: VREF at the nominal 3.30 V supply. Loose +/-5% sanity band only -- the +/-1% output-accuracy claim belongs to sim/output-voltage-tc/, not to this bench. Here it is the normalization reference and a check that the core was actually regulating during the sweep.

measurements.name: sweep_start_v
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the in-deck supply sweep really started at 2.97 V (-10%).

measurements.name: sweep_end_v
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the in-deck supply sweep really ended at 3.63 V (+10%).

measurements.name: n_supply_points
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the supply sweep produced the expected 31 points. If it silently collapsed to a single operating point, line_shift_mv would read 0 mV and look like a perfect pass.

spread_checks.note: The supply-induced shift must itself move by at least 0.05 mV across the process/temperature matrix. A dead-flat result would mean the corner include or .temp is not reaching the simulator.

notes: Supply is swept INSIDE the deck because the claim is about the shift across a range, not about any single supply point; the runner is therefore invoked with --supply 3.3 --subset-reason. Process and temperature run in full (5 x 3 = 15 points).
The corner axes above declare the full PVT matrix so the manifest stays the canonical statement of what the claim requires and the subset is visible as a subset in the record.
